summary_paragraph: A 30-year-old woman with Type 1 diabetes and a history of gastroparesis s/p gastric pacer presented with acute nausea and vomiting, one week after a prior hospitalization for similar symptoms. She had recently received a Botox injection for gastroparesis and reported coffee-ground emesis. She was admitted for inability to tolerate oral intake and managed with IV fluids, antiemetics (ondansetron, metoclopramide, compazine), and proton pump inhibition. Her hypertension, exacerbated by vomiting and anxiety, was controlled with IV metoprolol and transitioned to oral lisinopril. Abdominal imaging showed no obstruction or ileus. She gradually improved, tolerating a soft diet and oral medications. Her sodium was noted to be low (130) on discharge but asymptomatic; outpatient labs were ordered. She was discharged home in stable condition with new prescriptions for metoclopramide, pantoprazole, ondansetron, and lisinopril, and follow-up planned with gastroenterology for pacer evaluation.
problems: Diabetes with neurological manifestations, type I [juvenile type], not stated as uncontrolled
